caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 106 of 2010
lawyer:
SK. Awsafur Rahman, Advocate instructed by A. K. M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record -------- For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents ----- None represented.
parties:
Shaki Md. Shoaib and others. ------ Petitioners.
VS
Md. Kashem Ali Bhuiyan and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: In this petition for leave to appeal the petitioners have called in question the judgment and decree dated the 19th day of July, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 278 of 2003 allowing the same in part. 

 9. On Conclusion of hearing of the suit, the learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 22.04.2003 dismissed   the suit Against the judgment and  decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, the plaintiffs filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 278 of 2003 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division which heard the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the same in part i.e. decreed the suit for specific performance of contract in respect of 33 decimals of land out of suit plot No. 373; hence this petition for leave to appeal. 

 6. Mr. SK. Awsafur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners has contended that as per the undertaking executed by the plaintiffs on the date of execution of the agreement they offered TK. 3,00,000.00(three lakhs) to the defendant on 30.07.2000, that is, well within 1(one) month from the date of execution of the deed of agreement but he refused to accept the same saying that he would not sell the suit land to them and thus, the defendant failed to abide by the terms of the agreement which compelled the plaintiffs to file the suit. Mr. Awsafur Rahman has further contented that the plaintiffs were ready to perform, their part of the contract by paying the balance money which is apparent from the fact that they served a legal notice upon the defendant on 31.07.2000 (exhibit-2) asking him to accept TK. 3,00,000.00 from the plaintiffs within 7(seven) days from the date of receipt of the notice and execute and register the sale deed but the defendant by giving reply to the legal notice denied to execute and register the kabala on the plea that he entered into agreement to sell 33 decimals of land only, from suit plot number 373 at a consideration of TK. 4,25,000.00 and not to sell 2.44 acres of land, so the plaintiffs could not be blamed for non-payment of the balance consideration and thus to refuse to decree the suit as a whole. He has further contended that execution of the agreement having been admitted by the contesting defendant the onus was upon him to prove that he did not enter into the agreement to sell 2.44 acres of land but only 33 decimals of land which he failed to discharge, but the High Court Division failed to consider the said admitted factual aspect of the case in its proper perspective and thus, erred in law in not decreeing the suit as a whole, therefore, the impugned judgment and decree calls for interference by this Court by granting leaves. 

 7. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that it, on consideration of the evidence on record, came to the clear finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case that the defendant entered into the agreement with them to sell 2.44 acres of land. The trial Court believed the defendant's case that he executed the agreement to sell only 33 decimals of land from suit plot No. 373 at a consideration of TK. 4,25,000.00 and as part payment received TK. 2,00,000.00, but the plaintiffs made an agreement beyond the knowledge the defendant for the entire 2.44 acres of land which included homestead and graveyard. The trial Court also disbelieved plaintiffs case that they went to defendants house on 30.07.2000 to pay him TK. 3,00,000.00 (three lakhs) as per the alleged undertaking. The trial Court fur found that after agreement the defendant did not hand over possession of the suit land. The High Court Division concurring with the said findings of the trial. Court farther held that the plaintiffs failed to prove that they executed an undertaking to pay TK. 3,00,000.00/- to the defendant within 1 (one) month and that the plaintiffs offered any such money to the defendant. The High Court Division further held that the plaintiffs failed to prove that they ever offered to the defendant the balance consideration of TK. 29,42,500.00/- and thus performed their part as per terms of the agreement. However, the High Court Division allowed the appeal in part decreeing the suit in respect of 33 decimals of land only "appertaining to C.S. and S.A. Plot No. 373, described in item I of the suit schedule" on the admission of the defendant that he was ready to execute and register the sale deed in respect of the said area of land if he was paid the balance consideration of TK. 2,25,000.00/- by the plaintiffs. 

 9. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of Mr. Awsafur Rahman. Equally, we find no fault with the High Court Division in decreeing the l suit in respect of 33 decimals of land out of suit plot No. 373, as the defendant in his written statement admitted the fact of entering into agreement with the plaintiffs to sell the said area of land and while he examined himself as PW.1 also expressed his willingness to execute and register the kabala in respect of the said area of land subject to the payment of balance consideration by the plaintiffs. Further the defendant has not preferred any petition for leave to appeal before this Court against the part decree given by the High Court Division which shows that he has accepted the decree passed by the High Court Division.
